notes: All kept files are in their own folders under this directory with a source.json (page URL, download URL, page facts, download time). LICENCES: BigSoundBank items are CC0 (no attribution, commercial OK, not registered in Content ID). Mixkit items are under the Mixkit Sound Effects Free License (commercial use incl. online ads and broadcast OK, no attribution; you may not resell the raw file or register it with a rights-management/Content ID service). PROVENANCE ('real, not AI'): every BigSoundBank item is a documented recording (microphone, recorder and author listed on the page) except #2380, the aerospace beep, which the page labels 'Computer' (a plain 2,527 Hz sine tone made by the librarian - flagged in its entry). The Mixkit impacts and risers are human-made cinematic sound design (layered in a DAW: embedded tags show Logic Pro 9.1.8 / Logic Pro X with BWF dates 2014), not field recordings; for #2900, #1686, #1170, #163 and #1103 Mixkit gives no author or method and the files carry no metadata. Nothing here comes from an AI generator as far as can be determined, but Mixkit does not document it item by item. If strictly 'recorded' is required for the hit and riser, use #3179 thunder or #1023 distant cannon for the hit and the reversed #2312 cymbal for the riser. GAPS: (c) Geiger counter - no CC0/PD Geiger recording exists on BigSoundBank, Mixkit or Kenney; verified CC0 recordings on Freesound and a CC BY 3.0 one on Commons could not be downloaded from this sandbox (403 / 429) - see unavailable_candidates_not_downloaded for exact pages and licences. (f) a real NASA Quindar recording is listed there too; the BigSoundBank sine beep is the downloaded stand-in. MEASUREMENTS: ffprobe for format; ffmpeg ebur128 for integrated loudness and true peak; numpy on an ffmpeg float decode (mono sum) for sample peak, 5 ms / 10-100 ms RMS envelopes (dB relative to the loudest frame), band-energy shares and spectral centroid. 'SYNC' = time of the main transient (largest 10-20 ms level jump into the hit) or, for risers, the time of the peak where the hit should land. Integrated LUFS is unreliable for files under about 0.4 s. Suggested starting kit: pencil #221 (12-18 s) under the line drawing; grimoire page #362 on the notebook; Mixkit #790 riser ending on the logo frame with Mixkit #788's hit at 2.16 s (or #1686) layered with BigSoundBank #1023 for a real acoustic tail; Mixkit #1170 as an 8 s air swell under the radiation -> suit section. The pre-existing file client_camera_shutter.wav in this folder was not touched and is not part of this manifest. Not downloaded, possibly useful: NASA's 'Sounds from Beyond' page (https://www.nasa.gov/sounds-from-beyond/) hosts real Mars microphone recordings from Perseverance (e.g. wind on Mars, scam-mic-sol001-run001.wav); these are NASA/JPL-Caltech media, so check JPL's image/media use policy before using them in an ad.
